<details class="showcase-notes">
<summary>Model card: Model Showcase: Model Cards &amp; Results · slide 6</summary>

**Table.** Table 8.1.A, p. 167, summarizes the results. Sections 8.14.3 and 8.15.6 identify Fable’s configurations. The OSWorld evaluation uses the same revised task set for both models, a limit of 500 actions, and a 1080p desktop. Partial credit averages checkpoint completion within each task. Strict pass requires all checkpoints. AutomationBench uses the private evaluation set and requires all applicable assertions to pass. [Anthropic · Joint System Card, Table 8.1.A](https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/0339e6a7c5c7b87f5c07798616dc32c215d14235/Claude%20Fable%205.1%20&%20Claude%20Mythos%205.1%20System%20Card.pdf#page=167).

**Figure.** Anthropic, “A new performance frontier”, Terminal-Bench 4.0 table and accuracy–cost plot. The authors attribute part of the gap to earlier safeguards intervening on benchmark tasks. These figures measure the release configurations. Bars use a 0–100% scale. [Primary source](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1).

The workbook explicitly says Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are two configurations of one new LLM with the same weights. Mythos access requires verification programs. This relationship must not be read as a disclosure of dense versus MoE architecture. The tokenizer is inherited from Fable 5 and produces roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than models before Opus 4.7, according to the API changes recorded in the workbook.

Only Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 can read these thinking blocks. Editing earlier system messages, tools or conversation history invalidates the blocks. Text and images are inputs, and text is the output. Cache reads cost $0.25 per million tokens in this snapshot. The tools tile summarizes prompting guidance and API behavior, not additional intrinsic modules: batching independent tool calls can require a prompt nudge, and the subagent guide recommends asynchronous orchestration. Training remains Partial because the joint system card does not publish SFT, RL, optimizer or token-budget details.

**Snapshot and provenance.** LLM_v1.0.xlsx, sheet “Fable 5.1”, audit dated 18.10.2026. Category statuses follow “Сводка”: Architecture: Not disclosed; Data: Known; Training: Partial; Inference: Known; Tools: Known. Known means a model-specific fact is disclosed, not that the whole category is complete. These slides summarize the supplied audit and do not constitute a fresh independent verification. Prices, limits and availability refer to that snapshot.

**Source rows:** 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 17, 21, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40.

<details class="showcase-notes">
<summary>Results: Model Showcase: Model Cards &amp; Results · slide 7</summary>

Anthropic credits Claude Fable 5.1 with training a neural network for elevation reconstruction from Magellan radar. The images are the three aligned panels in the release’s “A small shield volcano on Venus” example. The 10–20 km number refers to the original altimetry footprint. The 300 m grid spacing is distinct from the estimated 2–3 km feature resolution. The Zenodo release covers about a third of Venus. Image credit is to the source article and the underlying NASA mission.

[Anthropic · Scientific research](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1). [Released elevation dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/22164484).

</details>
